translationRepairs: In the fifty-sixth year he was appointed prefect of Fengtian.
In the fifty-sixth year he was appointed prefectural governor (Fengtian yin) of Fengtian.
遷奉天府尹 names the special Fengtian prefectural governor (府尹), not an ordinary prefect (知府); the replacement restores that office.
In the fifty-sixth year he was transferred to be Fengtian prefect.
In the fifty-sixth year he was transferred to be Fengtian prefectural governor (Fengtian yin).
The literal field has the same error: 奉天府尹 is yin, not prefect; the proposed gloss matches the Chinese office.
Changzhou prefect Hu Guanlan associated with Salt Controller Zheng Rui's chief attendant Gao Bolin and imposed levies to repair Jiangyin's Guangfu Temple.
Changzhou prefect Hu Guanlan associated with Salt Controller Zheng Rui and his chief attendant Gao Bolin and imposed levies to repair Jiangyin's Guangfu Temple.
結交鹽政徵瑞長隨高柏林 names both Salt Controller Zheng Rui and attendant Gao Bolin as objects of 結交; the original genitive hides Zheng Rui as a mere modifier.

In the fifty-fourth year he was promoted to prefect of Chizhou in Anhui, repeatedly acted as intendant of Huai, Ningguo, Chizhou, and Taiping, managed the Wuhu customs house, kept none of the surplus for himself, and devoted it to famine relief.

In the fifty-fourth year he was promoted to prefect of Chizhou in Anhui, repeatedly acted as intendant of Huizhou, Ningguo, Chizhou, and Taiping, managed the Wuhu customs house, kept none of the surplus for himself, and devoted it to famine relief.
徽寧池太道 is the Huizhou–Ningguo–Chizhou–Taiping circuit (徽, not 淮); Huai is a different graph and place.
The court then wished to rectify grain transport; because governors Yue Qi and Daoqian both had reputations for integrity, it charged them to purge all abuses.
The court then wished to rectify grain transport; because Governor Yue Qi and Daoqian both had reputations for integrity, it charged them to purge all abuses.
巡撫岳起及道乾 attaches 巡撫 only to Yue Qi, then names Daoqian; plural “governors” invents that office for Daoqian.
When Suzhou, Lingbi, and Sizhou suffered floods, Jing Daoqian went in person to supervise the relief stations.
When Suzhou (Anhui), Lingbi, and Sizhou suffered floods, Jing Daoqian went in person to supervise the relief stations.
宿州 with 靈壁 and 泗州 is Anhui Suzhou, not Jiangsu 蘇州; the parenthetical prevents a false identification.
In the twenty-sixth year of Qianlong, a metropolitan graduate who ranked first in the palace examination, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
In the twenty-sixth year of Qianlong he became a metropolitan graduate, ranked first in the court examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
進士 and 朝考第一 are sequential: jinshi status, then first in the court examination for Hanlin selection, not first in the palace examination.

In recent years incompetent governors-general and governors have been exposed one after another; the high officials have all covered for one another, and prefectures and counties have also rushed to make deficits good.

In recent years incompetent governors-general and governors have been exposed one after another; the high officials have all striven to reform themselves, and prefectures and counties have also rushed to make deficits good.
共相濯磨 means scouring/self-reform after exposure, the reverse of covering for one another; the replacement matches that sense.
Pirates Cai Qian and Zhu Fen were then at their height. Governor Yu De was removed for negligence. Alinbao succeeded him but again clashed with Regional Commander Li Changgeng;
Pirates Cai Qian and Zhu Fen were then at their height. Governor-general Yu De was removed for negligence. Alinbao succeeded him but again clashed with Provincial Military Commander Li Changgeng;
總督玉德 is a governor-general and 提督李長庚 a provincial military commander; governor and regional commander are the wrong Qing ranks.
Cai Qian raided Kavalan on Taiwan's eastern coast, was driven off by aboriginal tribes, and asked that the territory be registered lest pirates occupy it.
Cai Qian raided Kavalan on Taiwan's eastern coast and was driven off by aboriginal tribes; Shicheng asked that the territory be registered lest pirates occupy it.
After the raid, silent 請 is the biographical subject Zhang Shicheng’s request to register Kavalan; attributing it to pirate Cai Qian inverts agent and motive.
Qian raided the rear of Taiwan at Kavalan, was repelled by raw savages, and requested that the land be brought into the registers lest pirates seize it.
Qian raided the rear of Taiwan at Kavalan and was repelled by raw savages; Shicheng requested that the land be brought into the registers lest pirates seize it.
請 is Zhang Shicheng’s silent-subject request, not Cai Qian’s, but bracketed “[Shicheng]” is awkward in the literal English; name him directly.
He was soon appointed Hanlin compiler; after his mourning period ended he was promoted to vice director of the Supervisorate of Education.
He was soon appointed Hanlin compiler; after his mourning period ended he was promoted to companion of the heir apparent (zhongyun).
中允 is an office of the heir apparent’s household, not the Supervisorate of Education; a bare pinyin title is accurate but not natural English.

Early in the Guangxu reign, Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general Wen Yu memorialized that Diantu's record as Fujian administration commissioner had been outstanding, and he received the posthumous title Wensu.
Early in the Guangxu reign, Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general Wen Yu memorialized that Diantu's former record in Fujian had been outstanding, and he received the posthumous title Wensu.
前任福建政績昭著 praises former service in Fujian generally and does not name the administration-commissioner post.
In the palace examination he was transferred to a secretary in the Ministry of Rites, served as chief examiner for the Guizhou provincial examinations, and rose in succession to bureau director.

In the Hanlin ranking examination he was transferred to a secretary in the Ministry of Rites, served as chief examiner for the Guizhou provincial examinations, and rose in succession to bureau director.
大考 after he is already a Hanlin reviser is the academicians’ ranking examination, not the palace examination that confers jinshi.
In the metropolitan examination he was transferred to a secretary in the Ministry of Rites, conducted the Guizhou provincial examinations, and rose in succession to bureau director.
In the ranking examination he was transferred to a secretary in the Ministry of Rites, conducted the Guizhou provincial examinations, and rose in succession to bureau director.
The same 大考 is not the metropolitan jinshi examination already recorded in the previous unit; “ranking examination” removes that false identification.
Yichou had long been childless. Once the case was resolved, his wife bore a son named Mingwan.
Yichou had long been childless. Once the case was resolved, he then had a son named Mingwan.
乃生子銘皖 makes Yichou the subject who then had a son; the original invents a wife as the person who bore the child.
Bandit gangs in eastern and western Guangdong are largely organized through this trade, and banditry has grown fiercer as a result.
Bandit gangs in Guangdong and Guangxi are largely organized through this trade, and banditry has grown fiercer as a result.
粵東西兩省 are the two Yue provinces, Guangdong and Guangxi, not eastern and western parts of Guangdong.
All bandit gangs in the two provinces of Guangdong are largely linked through this, causing the tide of banditry to grow fiercer.
All bandit gangs in the two provinces of eastern and western Yue (Guangdong and Guangxi) are largely linked through this, causing the tide of banditry to grow fiercer.
The literal “two provinces of Guangdong” collapses 粵東西兩省 into one province; the replacement restores Guangdong and Guangxi.

In the twenty-fourth year he died; the sovereign deeply regretted it, granted excellent edict condolence payments, posthumously gave him the rank of governor-general, and enfeoffed him with the posthumous title Gongjin.

In the twenty-fourth year he died; the sovereign deeply regretted it, granted excellent edict condolence payments, posthumously gave him the rank of governor-general, and bestowed on him the posthumous title Gongjin.
諡恭慎 confers a posthumous name; “enfeoffed” wrongly treats 諡 as a fief, which “bestowed” corrects.
